reviews.review:
The pros:
- I love a good sector-by-sector roguelike, and there are some pretty fun high risk / high reward mechanics to it.
- It does what's on the box which is real time squad management, I love Duskers but in that game it comes down to guesswork a lot of time, with no progression. This game has good algorithms for the people, and a good progression system.
- It's very satisfying to set up a squad member on overwatch in a key junction and have them be the guardian angel of your guys looting rooms.
- There are some fun mechanics from squad to squad, like a cybernetic squad that's very territory control, and another which encourages you to hunt down aliens for permanent random buffs to your guys.

The cons:
- I reached Senior Overseer in a little over 10 hours I think.
- The loadouts are prebaked (4 or 5 variants of 4 or 5 squads), so while it looks varied on the surface, there's not a lot of room for discovery and experimentation, like in Into the Breach for example. There are basically 3 classes of guys, and they have an ability that you can upgrade once, but it's always the same for the class.
- You might get one or two chances to upgrade your squad over the game, it's extremely rng. I have to decide at the beginning of the run if I want to take the path where I MIGHT be able to afford a melee weapon when I land on the melee weapon shop way down the line.
- The graphics are minimalistic, but even in Duskers you can see what your robots see. I just know that the circles are easy as pie to kill, and the X aliens are absolutely terrifying. I don't have one single idea what these aliens might actually look like.
- Speaking of the graphics, for a minimalistic game where my guys are dots on a screen, why does my graphics card make my laptop sound like it's going to take off when I run this game?? Is it fully rendering a 3d world I can't see? Is it mining bitcoin to max capacity??
- There are some dumb quality of life things that can be extremely frustrating. I have to tell myself "billy on bob" or whatever every single mission to remind myself to make the guy with the suppressing fire ability follow around the guy who hops into melee with the aliens the first chance he gets. I have to tell them this every single mission.
- The keyboard controls are extremely clunky. Many times have my guys died because I tried to use the recommended hotkeys to reference my squad members, only for it to mess up because one guy's already extracted. 90% of the time I used only the arrow keys, enter, and backspace.

Overall, I got enjoyment out of it but I wouldn't recommend. It feels like this game is missing some hardware optimization, and also some other gameplay elements, but I'm not sure what they are. Programmable start commands? Different missions like zone defense, stealth, boss fight in a revealed room? I think it's missing a lot of what I would expect out of a management game too, ship management, training between missions, more than one single predetermined skill upgrade? I don't know. It was a fun little game but it's maybe 30-40% of the way to being a game I would recommend to all my friends.
